Mr. Wang Ching Wei, Chairman of the Central Political Council, who passed through Hongkong yesterday, is due in Shanghai at 1 p.m. January 14 by the s.s. "Potsdam".

Acting on instructions from Mr. Lin Sen, President of the National Government, Dr. Chu Min Nyi, member of the Central Executive Committee of the Kuomintang, left Nanking for Shanghai by the 11 p.m. train yesterday to welcome Mr. Wang Ching Wei, who is due in Shanghai on January 14.

"SEVEN EVENTS SINCE THE NEW YEAR"

Looking through the reports published by this paper during the first seven days of the New Year, the following are the major events that have been given notice:-
1) On New Year Day, 10 Japanese warships fired machine guns towards the shore at Yanglinkow (杨林口), Zangzon (张泾).
2) At 11 a.m. January 2, a Japanese military aeroplane No.140 dropped small five-coloured flags together with absurd propaganda sheets at Tsingtao.
3) On the afternoon of January 2, three drunken Japanese marines assaulted a coolie and a foreign-dressed Chinese on Chapoo Road and Wuchang Road.
4) On January 3, two Japanese assaulted an umbrella hawker on Chengtu Road.
5) On the night of January 4, a Japanese special affairs organization at Chengchow was raided by the Chinese authorities. Secret documents disclosed a plot to create rioting with evil-doers. Three Japanese ronins were detained.
6) On January 5, the Chief of the Japanese Special Affairs Organization in Suiyuan knocked down a road worker in a motor car accident.
7) On January 7, six persons in Jehol were buried alive by Japanese gendarmes.
Most of the above events were due to persons who always talk of friendly relations with China. It gives one the headache to read these reports.
When they are in a happy mood, they pay some compensations for a murder or assault. (The case of the street worker who was knocked down in a motor car accident was settled with the payment of a compensation and medical expenses); sometimes a person who has been injured or killed gets nothing. The lives of Japanese, however, are precious and when they commit an offence, they are taken over by their own authorities as in the case of the three ronins who were arrested at Chengchow.

Japanese Warships Off Zangzoh

On the evening of January 1, more than ten Japanese warships appeared off Yang Lin (楊林) Harbour and Chi Ya (七丫) Harbour near Taichong (太倉) and discharged machine guns towards the shore for about half an hour. The ships left for up river the next morning.
According to information secured from the Peace Preservation Corps of Zangzoh, 14 Japanese warships passed the Dah Yuan (白苑) Harbour and the Ya Mou (野猫) Harbour at about 2 a.m. January 2. Two of them cruised between these two harbours and opened fire with machine guns towards the shore at the Ya Mou Harbour.
At about 3 p.m. January 2 a Japanese steamer arrived at Chung Sin (中心) Harbour and took soundings. A few marines landed and wandered about on shore. Residents near by together with Police officers advised them not to land or take soundings. The ship left after a party of soldiers was summoned from Kiengyin by telephone.

Great Crystal (大晶報), a mosquito paper :-

Some 10 Japanese warships opened fire towards the shore off Yang Lin near Zangzoh recently. Japanese aeroplanes in North China have been dropping absurd handbills.
The Japanese authorities have declared that it was only shooting practice; they pretended to know nothing about the dropping of handbills by Japanese aeroplanes in the North. Such actions on the part of the Japanese are liable to create ill-feeling among the Chinese people and to lead to trouble.
Since the liquidation of the Sian coup, intelligent Japanese are saying that Japan should change her policy towards China. Yet, the Japanese militarists still hold the view that a unified China would obstruct the expansion of Japanese militarism and that measures should be taken to prevent this.
In the interests of Japan herself, she should endeavour to make China co-operate with her for mutual existence and glory. Now is the time for the Japanese militarists to wake up and to cast aside all activities that are liable to incite ill-feeling among the Chinese people.

浏河附近的日本军舰

1月1日晚，十余艘日本军舰出现在太仓附近的杨林港和七丫港外，并向岸边发射机枪约半小时。次日清晨，这些舰只驶往上游。
据从浏河保安团获得的情报，1月2日凌晨2时许，14艘日本军舰经过白苑港和野猫港。其中两艘在这两个港口之间巡航，并在野猫港向岸边开火射击。
1月2日下午3时许，一艘日本汽船抵达中心港并进行测深。几名海军陆战队员上岸并在岸上四处游荡。附近居民会同警务人员劝告他们不要登陆或进行测深。在通过电话从江阴调来一队士兵后，该船离去。

小报《大晶报》称：

近日，约10艘日本军舰在浏河附近的杨林外向岸边开火。日本飞机在华北地区投撒荒谬的传单。
日本当局宣称这仅是射击演习；对于日本飞机在北方投撒传单一事，他们佯装不知。日本的此类行径容易在中国民众中引起恶感，并导致事端。
自西安事变平息以来，明智的日本人士认为日本应改变对华政策。然而，日本军国主义者仍持有一种观点，即统一的中国将阻碍日本军国主义的扩张，因此应采取措施加以阻止。
为了日本自身的利益，日本应努力使中国与其合作，以求共存共荣。现在是日本军国主义者觉醒并摒弃所有可能激起中国民众恶感的活动的时候了。

Mr. Fessendon, Secretary-General of the Shanghai
Municipal Council, and Mr. O.K. Yui, Chief Secretary of
the Shanghai City Government, have agreed upon a set of

Inspectorate will also be formed soon.

The Tung Nan Evening News (東南晚報) published on Jan.4
the following article contributed by one Sheh Ting Fong
(石廷芳):

"AN UNJUST POLICEMAN"

As I was walking along Chengtu Road on my
way to school, I noticed a crowd of people. I went up and
learned that it was some trouble between two hawkers, who
are business competitors. One of them had bribed a
policeman to find fault with the other every day. Noticing
that the policeman had failed to drive away the rival
hawker, the briber gave a further bribe to the officer
that day. As a result, the officer approached the rival
hawker and, after slapping him, dragged him to the Police
Station.
When I learned of the above, I reflected
that one day this policeman will be dismissed should
he continue to execute his duty in this unjust manner.

January 3, 1937.
Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers (Ningpo telegram) :-
GENERAL CHIANG KAI SHEK FLIES TO FENGHUA
General Chiang Kai Shek arrived at Ningpo
from Nanking by aeroplane at 10.20 a.m. January 2,
and later left by motor car for Fenghua to attend the
funeral of his brother. He was accompanied by Mr. Chen
Bu Lien.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers (Tsingtao telegram) :-
AEROPLANE OF "CERTAIN NATION" DROPS HANDBILLS AT TSINGTAO
At 11 a.m. January 2, an aeroplane of a
certain nation flew over Tsingtao and dropped handbills
containing baseless and absurd statements.
The Tsingtao City Government has lodged
a protest with the Japanese Consul.
At noon January 2, two Japanese military
aeroplanes flew to Tsingtao from Dairen and Tientsin
and returned soon after.

Peiping telegram :-
At noon January 2, a strange aeroplane
flew over Peiping and distributed similar handbills.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers (Zangzoh telegram) :-
OVER TEN JAPANESE WARSHIPS APPEAR OFF ZANGZOH
At noon January 2, the authorities at
Zangzoh received the following telephone message from
the Police Bureau at Taichong:- "On the afternoon of
January 1, more than ten Japanese warships anchored
off Chi Liao (七J), Yang Lin (楊林) and Ta Pang (大邦).
Heavy machine gunfire was heard. The armed forces
of the authorities at Taichong were mobilized, but
they did not return the fire for no instructions had
been received. The firing stopped after 30 minutes.
The warships left on the early morning of January 2."
The Zangzoh Hsien Government immediately
reported the matter to the higher authorities.
At 10 p.m. January 1, over ten Japanese
warships arrived at Fu Pu (許浦) and Ya Mou (野猫).
At the Ya Mou Harbour, the warships kept firing for
ten minutes. The warships left on the morning of
January 2.

Diary of Special Political Officer

November 24

The situation in Chapei remains quiet and
refugees continue to return although in small numbers.

No Sino-Japanese incidents of any note are
to be recorded. One very trifling occurrence
where a Japanese school boy made a much exaggerated report
of being assaulted by a Chinese on Pingliang Road has
unfortunately been taken up by the foreign press and
given a prominence which is by no means called for.

The China Weekly Review also sees fit in this
week's issue to disclose what it terms "Conspiracies
and frame-ups in the Nakayama Case". The article
is a violent attack on the Japanese Naval Landing
Party and may possibly prove harmful to future relations
between the Shanghai Municipal Police and the Japanese
Authorities. The article again is unfortunate in
that it comes on top of efforts of the S.M.P. to
secure a more liberal and more friendly exchange of views
and information with the Japanese Authorities in general
and Landing Party in particular.

J. H. Robertson
Special Political Officer

November 21.
The situation in Chapel remains quiet and refugees continue to return in small numbers.

At about 6 p.m. on November 21 a number of loafers assembled outside the Shanghai No. 3 Cotton Mill, a Japanese concern located at 31 Tsitsihar Road, and attempted by threats to dissuade the operatives as they emerged from working for a concern operated by Japanese. No report of the matter was received by the Municipal Police but on the following evening intimidation again occurred and was reported to the police with the result that five Chinese were arrested. Three of these were subsequently released for lack of evidence, while the remaining two were brought before the S.S.D. Court today when the police application for one week remand in custody was granted. There is a possibility that the prisoners are connected with some anti-Japanese movement although it is not unlikely that the incident is but a clumsy attempt at extortion.

Two cases of slogan writing on walls came to notice during the past 24 hours, one in Central District and the other in Changlu Road District. In both instances Chinese ink was used and the slogans were of the usual anti-Japanese nature.

J.W. Robertson
Special Political Officer

Diary of the Special Political Officer

November 19.
The situation in Chapei continues
normal although so far there has been no
noticeable return of residents who moved out
following the Darroch Road murder.

Only one case of slogan writing was
recorded yesterday. On a wall off Avenue Road
appeared written in Chinese ink the slogan :
"Declare war on Japan".

Between November 16 and 18 searches were
carried out on Court Warrant at nine Chinese
bookstores in the Settlement for anti-Japanese
publications. At six of these stores a total of
some 1,500 books were seized.

A conference attended by representatives
of the Municipal Police, Japanese Consulate-General
and Chinese Authorities was held at Municipal Police
Headquarters on November 18 when ways and means for
the coordination and more effective suppression of the
anti-Japanese movement were discussed. The meeting
resulted in better understanding among the respective
bodies and a closer and more effective co-operation
in dealing with subversive activities should result.

Min Pao published the following editorial on November 17 :-

EFFORTS TO CURB RUMOURS

Rumours have been very rife in Shanghai during
the past week, resulting in the suspension of the regular
curriculum of several schools, to say nothing of the heavy
losses sustained by the residents while evacuating. In view
of the fact that the spreading of rumours has had such a
serious effect upon the local conditions, the rumour mongers,
even if they have spread unfounded reports unintentionally,
should not be allowed to evade punishment for the offence
of circulating fabricated reports endangering the peace and
order of the community. The authorities should adopt rigid
measures to deal with those persons who are fabricating
rumours.
The Shanghai City Government has during the
past two days made every effort to curb the spreading of
rumours. This can be proved by the action adopted by the
Bureau of Public Safety in preventing shops from ceasing
operations, and residents from evacuating, and by the
Bureau of Education in prohibiting schools from suspending
their regular curriculum. All these are effective measures
in preventing the circulation of unfounded news. The action
adopted by the local Japanese Party in withdrawing their
marines from duty along the Extra Settlement roads constitutes
another help to calm down the public anxiety. As a result,
since November 16 public excitement has gradually diminished.
In our opinion, the authorities of the foreign
Settlements of Shanghai should co-operate closely and
thoroughly with the Shanghai City Government especially
at the time when the rumours begin to die away. The most
effective way to prevent traitorous elements from spreading
rumours is to adopt co-operative measures; while the prohibi-
tion of evacuation of residents should also be carried out
simultaneously and respectively. The practice of shouting
out alarming news by news vendors on streets that does not
correspond with the reports published in the newspapers
they are selling should be rigidly suppressed. Such practice
on the part of the news vendors is just as bad as that of
those traitorous characters who disseminate fabricated
reports.
It is also be hoped that the authorities concerned
will adopt appropriate measures to prohibit the newspapers
and other publications from publishing unreliable information
and alarming reports with a view to improving friendship and
calming down the unsettled state of the residents. Unless
concentrated efforts are made by all parties in curbing
these rumours and tranquilizing the public excitement,
no effective result can be achieved.

只有向强国提出呼吁才能得到考虑，但对于

《民报》于11月17日发表以下社论：

遏制谣言的努力

过去一周，上海谣言四起，导致几所学校
停课，更不用说居民在撤离期间遭受的巨大损失。鉴于
谣言的传播对当地局势产生了如此严重的影响，即使
造谣者是无心地传播了毫无根据的报道，也不应允许
他们逃避因散布 fabricated 报告、危害社区和平与秩序
而受到的惩罚。当局应采取严厉措施对付那些制造
谣言的人。
上海市政府在过去两天里竭尽全力遏制
谣言的传播。公安局采取措施防止商店停业
和居民撤离，教育局禁止学校停课，这些行动
都证明了这一点。所有这些都是防止毫无根据的消息
流传的有效措施。当地日本方面采取行动，将其海军陆战队

我们认为，上海外国租界当局应与上海市政府
密切且彻底地合作，特别是在谣言开始平息的时候。
防止奸分子散布谣言的最有效方法是采取合作措施；

叫卖与其所售报纸刊登的报道不符的惊人消息的做法，
应予以严厉取缔。报贩的这种行径与那些散布虚假
报道的奸徒一样恶劣。
也希望有关当局采取适当措施，禁止报纸
和其他出版物发布不可靠的信息和令人恐慌的报道，
以改善友谊并平息居民的不安状态。除非各方集中
努力遏制这些谣言并平息公众的激动情绪，否则
无法取得有效成果。

Diary of Special Political Officer. No. 8.

Nov. 16. There is nothing new to record in the local
situation and during the past twenty four hours the
influx of refugees from Chapei and adjacent areas
by way of roads in the northern district and bridges
in the eastern area continued unabated. The Chinese
Authorities have done everything to persuade these
people to remain quietly in their houses but these
efforts have proved abortive in the face of the many
terrorist rumours current. That the refugees should turn
a deaf ear to reason is perhaps pardonable when rumour
mongers make capital of the appearance in Hangwai North
Station on the forenoon of November 14 of a Japanese
landing party patrol of twenty six unarmed men and on
Boundary Road on November 15 of two motor cycles manned
by Japanese naval ratings. The presence of these parties
is not altogether consistent with the claim of Chief
Staff Officer Yasuda that the Landing Party cannot in
any way be blamed for the exodus of refugees from Chapei.

OBSERVATION MADE IN CHAPEI THIS MORNING, HOWEVER,
SHOWS A GREAT IMPROVEMENT IN THE REFUGEE SITUATION AND
IT MAY BE SAID THAT EVACUATION HAS NOW CEASED. The
Chinese Authorities are making every effort to reassure
those residents who still remain. It is difficult to
give with any accuracy statistics of people who have
evacuated Chapei and adjacent areas since the unrest
commenced but, summing up reports from observations
made at various points, a reasonable estimate is possible
in the neighbourhood of 40,000.

11月16日。本地局势无新情况可记录，在过去二十四小时内，来自闸北及邻近地区的难民经由北区道路和东区桥梁持续不断地涌入。中国当局已竭尽全力劝说这些人安静地留在家中，但在目前流传的许多恐怖谣言面前，这些努力均告失败。当造谣者利用11月14日上午二十六名 unarmed（未武装）人员组成的日本登陆队巡逻队出现在虹口北站，以及11月15日两名由日本海军水兵驾驶的摩托车出现在界路（Boundary Road）一事大做文章时，难民们对理性劝告充耳不闻或许是可以原谅的。这些人员的出现，与安藤（Yasuda）首席参谋官声称登陆队对闸北难民外逃不负任何责任的說法并不完全一致。

November 16, 1935. Morning Translation

China Times(Nanking telegram) :-

War Minister Refutes Groundless Rumours in Shanghai

When approached by the reporters of the Central News Agency, General Ho Yin Ching, Minister of War, stated that as Shanghai is a place where all races reside, it is naturally easy to circulate rumours. Speculators often make rumour spreading a profession, having no regard for the good of the country. The Central Government, he added, has adopted a friendly policy towards Japan in order to improve relations between these two countries. This policy has not been changed in any way. Therefore the Shanghai rumours are all unfounded. Cool minded persons ought never to be misled by rumours.

Shun Pao(Current Comment):-

Rumours

Since the case of the murder of a Japanese marine in Shanghai, the city and surrounding districts are full of rumours. The area where the Shanghai War was fought has been evacuated by the residents who fled to the Southern Settlement area in confusion. Household removing trucks and other cars were hired even up to the very last one, during the past two days. Some people even removed their property in the middle of the night. Such an evacuation not only causes the people to sustain financial losses and prevents the rehabilitation of Chapel, but the foreign relations with China will also be affected.

Undoubtedly, the present nonsensical movement is due to the careless credance by the citizens in unfounded rumours. There are two reasons why such rumours are believed:-
(1) The memory of the lamentable Shanghai War is recalled by the murder of a Japanese marine.
(2) Not long after the promulgation of the new monetary system, various important leaders assemble at Nanking to discuss unity in the 5th National Congress of the Kuomintang.

The above two occurrences are important affairs affecting the country. Speculators take advantage of these occasions to make all sorts of guesses which are believed as being true by citizens who have little or no sense.

Now, General Ho Yin Ching, Minister of War, has made a substantial denial of the truth of any of these rumours, and the Shanghai City Authorities are making every effort to pacify the people. It is hoped that these rumours will soon cease to be heard.

《中国时报》（南京电）：-

陆军部长驳斥上海无稽谣言

当中央通讯社记者采访陆军部长何应钦将军时，他表示，上海是各族杂居之地，自然容易传播谣言。投机商常以散布谣言为业，不顾国家利益。他补充说，中央政府为改善中日两国关系，对日本采取友好政策。这一政策没有任何改变。因此，上海的谣言纯属无稽之谈。头脑冷静的人绝不应被谣言所误导。

《申报》（时事评论）：-

谣言

自从上海发生日本海军陆战队员被杀案以来，全市及周边地区谣言四起。曾为淞沪战场的地区，居民混乱逃往南市租界区域，导致该地区人口清空。过去两天内，搬家卡车和其他车辆甚至被租赁一空。有些人甚至在半夜搬运财产。这种撤离不仅使人民遭受经济损失，阻碍闸北的恢复重建，而且也会影响中国的对外关系。

毫无疑问，目前这种荒谬的举动是由于市民轻率地轻信无稽谣言所致。人们相信此类谣言有两个原因：-
(1) 日本海军陆战队员被杀案唤起了人们对惨痛的淞沪战争的记忆。
(2) 在新币制颁布后不久，各位重要领袖聚集南京，讨论国民党第五次全国代表大会上的团结问题。

上述两件事是影响国家的重要事务。投机商利用这些时机进行各种猜测，而被缺乏理智的市民信以为真。

现在，陆军部长何应钦将军已实质性地否认了这些谣言的真实性，上海市政府当局正尽力安抚民心。希望这些谣言能很快平息。

Journal de Shanghai:

CHINA'S ATTITUDE TOWARDS JAPAN WILL BE STIFFENED---
AUTHORS OF THE ATTEMPT ON WANG CHING WEI ARE HIS
FORMER PARTISANS

(From our special correspondent)

Nanking, November 14.

China has arrived at the turning point
in her history. Reunification appears to be at the
point of realization, after four years of preaching.
The presence at the 5th National Congress of the principal
leaders of the Opposition would seem to indicate that
Chiang Kai Shek has already accepted in theory the
principles of Hu Han Min regarding the foreign and
domestic policy of China. Hu Han Min is embarking for
China on the 15th at Marseille or Genoa.

------------------

For the first time in four years, that
is to say, since the commencement of the Sino-Japanese
conflict, the Press of Chiang Kai Shek is openly
criticising the foreign policy of the Central Government,
calling it a policy of indecision and declaring it to be
the principal cause of the uneasiness, the nervousness
and discontent among the people.
For the first time also, the "Shanghai
Morning Post", the organ of Chiang Kai Shek, has openly
discussed the question or war or peace with Japan in an
editorial this morning entitled "Peace or War".
After condemning the wavering policy of
the Central Government towards Japan, the paper declares
that China has only two courses open to her: war or
peace with Japan. A war would be horrible, but the
sufferings which China would have to endure as a result
of a humiliating peace and foreign domination would be
worse than all the horrors of a sanguinary war.
The tone of this editorial is very
significant and great importance is being attached to it.
In the course of conversation with a
Chinese politician, the latter declared, "The Chinese
people desire to be sincerely at peace with Japan, but
their patience is exhausted. Certainly we shall not
refuse genuine and sincere collaboration with Japan, but
this collaboration, as we have not ceased to reiterate,
must be based on complete equality. The Chinese people
will never pardon the Government should it accept any
humiliating demands."

The 5th National Congress will decide
the future destiny of China, for it will have to determine
the future foreign and domestic policy of the country.
Although the results of the exchange of views between
the influential leaders of the Kuomintang are yet unknown,
it seems clear that the attitude of China towards Japan
will be stiffened in future.
It is probable that the present Congress
will fix a date in 1937 for the convocation of the People's
National Assembly.

《上海日报》：

中国对日态度将趋于强硬——刺杀汪精卫者为其昔日追随者

（本报特约记者）

南京，11月14日。

中国已到达其历史的转折点。经过四年的宣扬，统一似乎即将实现。反对派主要领导人出席第五次全国代表大会，似乎表明蒋介石在理论上已经接受了胡汉民关于中国内外政策的原则。胡汉民将于15日从马赛或热那亚启程回国。

------------------

四年来，即自中日冲突开始以来，蒋介石方面的报纸首次公开批评中央政府的对外政策，称其为犹豫不决的政策，并宣称这是造成民众不安、焦虑和不满的主要原因。
同样也是首次，蒋介石的机关报《上海晨报》在今早一篇题为《和平还是战争》的社论中，公开讨论了与日本战或和的问题。
该报在谴责中央政府对日摇摆不定的政策后宣称，中国只有两条路可走：与日本开战或言和。战争固然可怕，但中国因屈辱的和平及外国统治而必须承受的苦难，将比血腥战争的所有恐怖更甚。
这篇社论的语气非常意味深长，受到极大重视。
在与一位中国政治家的谈话中，后者表示：“中国人民真诚希望与日本和平相处，但他们的耐心已耗尽。当然，我们不会拒绝与日本进行真正和诚恳的合作，但这种合作，正如我们要不断重申的那样，必须建立在完全平等的基础上。如果政府接受任何屈辱性的要求，中国人民永远不会原谅它。”

第五次全国代表大会将决定中国的未来命运，因为它必须确定国家未来的内外政策。虽然国民党有影响力领导人之间交换意见的结果尚不得而知，但显然，中国未来对日本的态度将会强硬起来。
本届大会很可能会确定在1937年召开国民大会的日期。

THE SINO-JAPANESE TENSION
(Editorial)

During the past few days, Hongkew and Chapei
have been thrown into a state of great excitement. Large
numbers of Chinese families have removed from these
areas where, in 1932, sanguinary fighting had taken place.
It is certain that their fears are exaggerated
and there is no reason to expect another war at the gates
of Shanghai. The present exodus is being caused by the
reappearance of certain unpleasant signs which have
terrified the inhabitants of Chapei and Hongkew and
the dissemination of false reports by unknown people
which have alarmed a naturally credulous population.
On the other hand, incidents have occurred
which, in themselves, are of no grave import but which
have caused great uneasiness coming as they do at a
time when the relations between China and Japan have
once become strained.
We do not say that there is a relation of
cause and effect between the most important of those
incidents and the Sino-Japanese discord which has arisen
over the recent financial measures adopted by the Nanking
Government and the political changes that are looming in
China. The author of the shooting in Darroch Road has not
yet been discovered and nobody knows anything of the
motive of the crime. In ordinary times, little attention
would have been given to the affair, but to-day it has
provoked intervention by the Japanese Naval Authorities
as well as by the Japanese Embassy and Consulate-General
while great discontent has been aroused among the Japanese
community in Shanghai.

中日紧张局势
（社论）

在过去几天里，虹口和闸北陷入了极大的骚动之中。大量中国家庭从这些地区搬离，1932年这里曾发生过血腥战斗。
可以肯定的是，他们的恐惧被夸大了，没有理由预期上海城门口会再次爆发战争。目前的逃离潮是由于某些令人不快的迹象再次出现，吓坏了闸北和虹口的居民，以及不明人士散布虚假报告，惊扰了天生轻信的民众。
另一方面，也发生了一些事件，这些事件本身并不严重，但由于发生在中日关系再次紧张的时刻，引起了极大的不安。
我们并不说那些最重要的事件与因南京政府最近采取的金融措施和中国 looming（逼近/显现）的政治变化而产生的中日不和之间存在因果关系。达罗克路枪击案的凶手尚未被发现，无人知晓犯罪动机。在平时，人们很少会关注此事，但今天它引发了日本海军当局以及日本大使馆和总领事馆的干预，并在上海日侨社区中引起了极大的不满。

Normally, the smashing of the windows of
a Japanese shop on Nanking Road would have passed unnoticed,
but coming, as it has, after the first incident, the
affair has given rise to bitter discussions between the
Settlement authorities and the Japanese, with the latter
declaring that the Police are not according sufficient
protection to them. It is also reported that Japanese
children have been assaulted by Chinese. Stupidity can
be their only excuse, nevertheless such acts are deplorable
and will only accentuate the present situation.
As for the change in the relations between
China and Japan, it has been noticeable since the first
few days of the present month. The attempted assassination
of Wang Ching Wei has given rise to much uneasiness to
Tokyo and it was asked whether even the temporary elimina-
tion of Wang Ching Wei would permit the opponents of Sino-
Japanese understanding to gain the upper hand. Inspired
by the authorities, the Press published warnings to China
in order to make her understand that Japan would not
modify her views and would energetically follow the
policy fixed since the Tangku Armistice.
Then came the Chinese monetary reform which
has increased Japan's bad humour. There was great
indignation in official Japanese circles.
Now, according to news from Nanking,
China, after the 5th National Congress, will show herself
less docile towards Japan. If she does not openly adopt
a policy of resistance, she will not show herself less
determined. Such is the impression created by the
reconciliation between Nanking and Canton. At Nanking,
a changed atmosphere has been noticeable during the past
few months.
It is not at all certain whether a
"policy of firmness" will provoke a conflict. Japan knows
what she wants and in all likelihood she is determined to
get it. But perhaps there is a way to reach an understanding
by means of a formula and a method acceptable to both
parties.
The excitement in Shanghai to-day is due
to the tension in the political relations between the two
countries. The excitement will die out immediately if
the relations between Nanking and Tokyo become satisfactory,
an eventuality which, after all, is not unrealizable.

通常，南京路上一家日本商店的窗户被砸碎本不会引起注意，但由于发生在第一起事件之后，此事引起了租界当局与日本人之间的激烈争论，后者声称警察未给予他们足够的保护。另有报道称，日本儿童遭到中国人袭击。愚蠢是他们唯一的借口，尽管如此，此类行为令人遗憾，只会加剧目前的局势。
至于中日关系的变化，自本月头几天以来就已显而易见。汪精卫遇刺未遂事件在东京引起了极大的不安，有人询问，即使是汪精卫的暂时出局，是否会让反对中日谅解的人占据上风。在当局的授意下，报纸发表了对中国的警告，使其明白日本不会改变其观点，并将有力地遵循自《塘沽停战协定》以来确定的政策。
随后是中国货币改革，这加剧了日本的不满情绪。日本官方圈子对此极为愤怒。
现在，根据来自南京的消息，中国在第五次全国代表大会之后，对日本的表现将不再那么顺从。如果她不公开采取抵抗政策，她也不会表现出决心减弱。这就是宁粤和解所造成的印象。在南京，过去几个月的气氛发生了变化。
“强硬政策”是否会引发冲突尚不确定。日本知道自己想要什么，而且很可能决心得到它。但也许有一种方法可以通过双方都能接受的公式和方法达成谅解。
上海今天的骚动是由于两国政治关系的紧张所致。如果南京和东京之间的关系变得令人满意，这种骚动将立即平息，而这毕竟并非不可能实现。

G. M.

新货币政策

第一特区市民联合会昨日致函工部局及公共安全局：
“为巩固国家财政，国民政府于11月4日颁布新货币政策，将中央银行、中国银行和交通银行的钞票转换为法定货币。这一政策得到全国人民的拥护。
然而，虹口的一些奸商和游手好闲之徒受他人指使，以高价向民众收购白银。近来这类奸商的数量大幅增加。
请予逮捕并惩处。”

小报《上海报》发表评论如下：

中国的不安

自从朝日飞机访华以及国民政府发布与各国保持友好关系的命令以来，中日亲善的趋势逐渐增加。两国人民组织了相互视察团进行互访。因此，中日合作稳步进展。然而，出乎意料的是，近几日各地谣言四起，导致民众非常不安。
局势变化何其迅速！
这些最近的谣言源于日本在大连、青岛、上海和台湾举行的军事会议，以及日本军事当局在北平非法逮捕中国人。这些引起了民众的不安，构成了中日合作未来的严重障碍。
关于最近在上海发生的一名日本海军陆战队士兵被杀案，虽然这是一起严重的罪行，但案件发生在租界以外的道路上。至于凶手是谁，案件的底细如何，尚不清楚。日本报纸和日本居民不考虑基本细节，从而引发了各种谣言，导致闸北居民外逃。因此，日本的举动让我们深感遗憾。
关于中日亲善，自然会受到我们的欢迎。然而，如果我们想达到真正亲善的目的，双方都应真诚。如果一方竭尽全力推进亲善，而另一方却处处阻挠，则无法达到任何目的。例如，最近的

胡汉民启程回国

November 15, 1935.
Morning Translation.

Chen Pao (Shanghai Morning Post, an official organ of General Chiang Kai Shek) publishes the following editorial:-

RUMOURS

Since the occurrence of the murder of a Japanese marine in Hongkew, Japanese newspapers have criticized the Chinese Authorities at will and have also disseminated propaganda to the effect that the Japanese Landing Party Authorities have already passed a final decision. Civilians in the vicinity of Chapei have become alarmed and many rumours have begun to circulate. It seems that a second January 28 Incident will soon take place. As a consequence, the evacuation of residents from Chapei is increasing daily, notwithstanding the refutation of the rumours by the Shanghai City Government. Although residents in Chapei became alarmed at the occurrence of the murder of the Japanese marine, yet there were many unfounded rumours that had been in circulation previously. The Nanking Road case also, wherein a Japanese firm was attacked, caused Chapei residents, who had learned a lesson during the January 28 Incident, to become panic stricken.

Rumours relating to the question of China and Japan have been in circulation during the past several years, but they increased after the outbreak of the Italo-Abyssinian hostilities. Someone said that Great Britain was not in a position to bother about affairs in the Far East and that Japan could do what she liked. The report that Japan had submitted 13 demands to China was then circulated, this being followed later by another rumour that Japan had presented 8 demands to China. The people think that Japan is aiming at demands similar to the "21 demands" to China, and fear that a critical stage is forthcoming. Such is not however the case. If we could analyse the situation of the world, we would be convinced that Japan could attack China at any moment she liked, and there is no necessity for her to wait until the outbreak of the Italo-Abyssinian War. That Great Britain is unable to deal with the situation in the Far East has already been disclosed to the world during the Sino-Japanese Hostilities in Shanghai, and the Japanese are well aware of this fact.

Rumours have also been current for some time to the effect that Japan has demanded that she be permitted to send delegates to attend the 6th Plenary Session of the C.E.C. of the Kuomintang as well as the 5th National Congress of the Party. The 6th Plenary Session has been concluded and the 5th National Congress is now being held in Nanking, but we did not see any Japanese delegates at those meetings. （印：... OF POLICE ... NOV. 1935 ... SHANGHAI）

According to the Shanghai Mainichi, there have arisen during the past two months more than 20 kinds of rumours concerning the activities of Japan and China. Therefore, when the Darroch Road Incident occurred, the anxiety of the people reached a maximum.

The Japanese papers have pointed out that these rumours are fabricated by Chinese and are entirely groundless. It proves that for the time being Japan has no intention to create any trouble and people may consequently rest assured that there will be no outbreak of hostilities.

《晨报》（蒋介石将军的官方机关报）发表如下社论：-

谣言

自从虹口发生一名日本海军陆战队员被杀事件以来，日本报纸随意批评中国当局，并散布宣传称日本登陆部队当局已做出最终决定。闸北附近的平民感到恐慌，许多谣言开始流传。似乎第二次“一·二八”事变即将发生。因此，尽管上海市政府对谣言进行了辟谣，但从闸北撤离的居民仍日益增多。虽然闸北居民因日本海军陆战队员被杀事件而感到恐慌，但此前已有许多毫无根据的谣言在流传。南京路案件（一家日本公司遭到袭击）也使在“一·二八”事变中吸取了教训的闸北居民陷入恐慌。

有关中日问题的谣言在过去几年中一直流传，但在意阿敌对行动爆发后有所增加。有人说英国无暇顾及远东事务，日本可以为所欲为。随后流传出日本向中国提出13项要求的报道，此后又出现另一则谣言，称日本向中国提出了8项要求。民众认为日本旨在提出类似对华“二十一条”的要求，并担心危急关头即将到来。然而事实并非如此。如果我们分析世界局势，就会确信日本可以随时攻击中国，没有必要等到意阿战争爆发。英国无力应对远东局势的情况，在上海的中日敌对行动期间已向世人披露，日本人对此事实十分清楚。

此外，一段时间以来一直有谣言称，日本要求允许派遣代表参加国民党第六届中央执行委员会全体会议以及党的第五次全国代表大会。六中全会已结束，五全大会正在南京举行，但我们并未在这些会议上看到任何日本代表。（印：... 警务处 ... 1935年11月 ... 上海）

据《上海每日新闻》报道，过去两个月出现了20多种有关中日活动的谣言。因此，当达罗克路（Darroch Road）事件发生时，民众的焦虑达到了顶点。

日本报纸指出，这些谣言是由中国人捏造的，完全毫无根据。这证明日本目前无意制造任何麻烦，民众可以放心，不会爆发敌对行动。

November 15, 1935. Morning Translation.

The present unrest is, beyond doubt, the
result of rumours, which were fabricated under certain
conditions. The most important of these conditions
is the ever uncertain attitude which the Japanese adopted
towards us. The Japanese ambition to procure one thing
after another is deeply impressed in our minds.
Therefore, whenever any rumour starts regarding any
movement of the Japanese, it spreads far and fast,
because our Chinese are like birds who have already
been scared by being shot at. Secondly, the new
exhausted Communist Party is making a final attempt to
throw China into confusion. The Communists purposely
organize the spreading of all sorts of rumours. At the
same time, they are employing every kind of method in
attempting to provoke another January 28 Incident.
Thirdly, landlords, for the purpose of raising their
land value and house rents, may have taken advantage of
the situation to spread the rumours in the hope that the
demand for houses in the Settlements would be increased.
Now, if these rumours are to be quelled, it is first
necessary for a complete change to take place in the
Japanese attitude towards China, secondly, our Government
should make public all recent negotiations between China
and Japan in order to bring about the peace of mind of
the people, thirdly, Chinese people should recognize
their individual duty towards their country. They
should consider the general situation of the country and
not resort to emotional actions creating unnecessary
disturbances. Slightly emotional actions by the people
of strong nations may produce no great harm, but in the
case of weak nations such actions may lead to unfortunate
incidents.

Min Pao and other local newspapers :-

Five Rumour Mongers Arrested by Bureau of Public
Safety

During the last few days rumours have been
very rife in Chapei from where large numbers of residents
have evacuated into the Settlements.
When interviewed by a reporter of the
Central News Agency yesterday, Liang Fu Tso, Chief of
the North Station Branch of the Bureau of Public Safety
stated that such rumours were ostensibly spread by some
illiterate idlers. The situation in Chapei is quite
calm. As the spreading of such rumours constitutes a
grave danger to the maintenance of peace and order of
this locality, he has, therefore, issued strict
instructions to his various subordinates to attempt to
arrest these rumours mongers. The residents should
remain at ease and should not be taken in by such
unfounded news. He further stated that five such
unscrupulous persons had been arrested and were found
to be all illiterate people.

目前的动荡无疑是谣言的结果，这些谣言是在特定条件下捏造的。其中最重要的条件是日本对我们采取的态度始终不确定。日本贪得无厌的野心给我们留下了深刻印象。因此，每当有关于日本动向的谣言出现时，它就会迅速广泛传播，因为我们中国人就像惊弓之鸟。其次，新近受挫的共产党正做最后尝试，企图使中国陷入混乱。共产党人故意组织散布各种谣言。同时，他们采用各种方法试图引发另一次“一·二八”事变。第三，房东为了提高土地价值和房屋租金，可能利用局势散布谣言，希望增加对租界房屋的需求。现在，如果要平息这些谣言，首先必须彻底改变日本对华态度，其次，我国政府应公布最近中日之间的所有谈判，以使民众安心，第三，中国人民应认识到个人对国家的责任。他们应考虑国家大局，不要采取情绪化行动造成不必要的骚乱。强国人民的轻微情绪化行动可能不会产生巨大危害，但在弱国的情况下，此类行动可能导致不幸事件。

《民报》及其他本地报纸：-

公安局逮捕五名造谣者

过去几天，闸北谣言甚嚣尘上，大量居民从那里撤离进入租界。
昨天在接受中央社记者采访时，公安局北站分局局长梁福佐表示，这些谣言表面上是由一些不识字的闲散人员散布的。闸北局势相当平静。由于散布此类谣言对该地区和平秩序的维护构成严重危险，因此他已向各下属发出严格指令，试图逮捕这些造谣者。居民应保持镇定，不要被此类毫无根据的消息所欺骗。他还表示，五名此类不法分子已被逮捕，经查均为文盲。

November 15, 1935. Morning Translation.

Min Pao and other local newspapers :-

SHANGHAI CITY GOVERNMENT OFFERS $1,000 REWARD FOR THE
APPREHENSION OF THE ASSASSIN OF A JAPANESE MARINE

With a view to bringing about an early
apprehension of the assailant in connection with the murder
of Hideo Nakayama, First Class Japanese Marine of the local
Japanese Landing Party, at the Extra Settlement Roads,
the Shanghai City Government has offered a reward of $1,000
for the arrest of this culprit and has ordered the Bureau
of Public Safety to effect his apprehension within a
specified time.
It is learned that the Shanghai Municipal
Police has adopted similar measures for the apprehension
of this culprit.

Min Pao and other local newspapers :-

SHANGHAI 1ST SPECIAL DISTRICT CITIZENS FEDERATION WARNS
ITS MEMBERS AGAINST UNDESIRABLE DISPUTES

Yesterday the Shanghai 1st Special District
Citizens Federation sent the following circular letter to
its various branches:-
"We are in receipt of a circular order
No. 1403 from the Bureau of Social Affairs, which reads
as follows:-
'Acting upon instructions from the
Shanghai City Government, your Federation is
instructed to notify your various branches and
members to take every precaution against any
undesirable disputes which are likely to affect the
peace and order of the local community. Violators
of these instructions will be arrested and severely
dealt with.'
"In view of the above, you are instructed

《民报》及其他本地报纸：-

上海市政府悬赏1000元缉拿杀害日本海军陆战队员的凶手

为了早日抓获在当地日本登陆部队一等兵中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）于越界筑路地区被杀一案中的袭击者，上海市政府已悬赏1000元缉拿此罪犯，并命令公安局在规定期限内将其抓获。

上海第一特区市民联合会警告会员避免不当争端

昨天，上海第一特区市民联合会向其各分会发送了如下通函：-
“我们收到社会局第1403号通令，内容如下：-
‘奉上海市政府指令，贵会须通知各分会及会员，采取一切预防措施，防止任何可能影响当地社区和平秩序的不当争端。违反本指令者将被逮捕并严惩。’

Nov mber 15, 1935. Morning Translation.

NIPPO

S.M.C. ESTABLISHES SPECIAL SECTION IN THE POLICE
FORCE TO DEAL WITH ANTI-JAPANESE ACTIVITIES

Yesterday the S.M.C. issued
a wanted notice offering $1,000 for information leading
to the arrest of the murderer of Nakayama, first
class marine, and at the same time a special section
was established in the S.M.P. consisting of one
European and one Japanese Assistant Commissioner of
Police who have been appointed to deal with all anti-
Japanese activities.

REPORT ON THE MURDER OF NAKAYAMA TO BE MADE TO
ADMIRAL HYAKUTAKE

Vice-Admiral Hyakutake,
Commander of the Japanese Third Fleet, will arrive in
Shanghai at 5 a.m. November 15 on the temporary flagship
"Kuma" which will be moored alongside the S.S.K.
Wharf. At 9 a.m. the Kuma will be relieved from
the duty of flagship by the "Idzumo".
Staff officer Yasuda of the
Shanghai Special Landing Party and Naval Attache Okino
will call on Vice-Admiral Hyakutake on the "Idzumo"
and make a report on the murder of first class marine,
Nakayama.
The Senior naval officials
will hold a conference to consider the incident.

19TH ROUTE ARMY MATCHES TO BE CONFISCATED

Owing to the prevailing
anti-Japanese activities, the chief of the Shanghai
City Social Bureau has decided to suppress the selling
of 19th Route Army matches and has informed the Chinese
Match Dealers Federation accordingly. The Chinese
Match Dealers Federation held a conference on November
13 and 14 to consider the matter. As a result it
was decided to confiscate and destroy all 19th Route
Army matches as from 2 p.m. November 15.

MEETING OF JAPANESE RESIDENTS CORPORATION

At noon yesterday the Foreign
Affairs Negotiations Committee of the Japanese Residents
Corporation held a meeting to discuss the murder of
Nakayama, first class marine. As regards the murder
case it was decided to leave the matter in the hands of
the Japanese authorities and all residents should devote
themselves peacefully to their business.
As regards the Nanking Road
incident it was decided to request the punishment of the
policemen who were on duty near the scene of the riot for
neglecting their duty and for failing to effect any
arrests, and also to request the punishment of the officer
who was supervising these policemen.
The Committee also decided to
hold an emergency meeting any time the situation calls
for such, besides the regular weekly meetings.

《日日新闻》

工部局在警务处设立特别科以对付反日活动

关于中山被杀案的报告将呈报百武副司令

日本第三舰队司令百武三郎海军少将将于11月15日上午5时乘坐临时旗舰“熊野”号抵达上海，该舰将停靠在S.S.K.码头。上午9时，“出云”号将接替“熊野”号担任旗舰。
上海特别登陆部队参谋安田和海军武官奥野将登上“出云”号拜会百武海军少将，并就一等兵中山被杀案作出报告。
海军高级官员将举行会议审议此事。

没收十九路军火柴

由于反日活动盛行，上海市社会局局长决定禁止销售十九路军火柴，并已通知中国火柴商联合会。中国火柴商联合会于11月13日和14日召开会议审议此事。结果决定自11月15日下午2时起，没收并销毁所有十九路军火柴。

日本居留民团会议

昨天中午，日本居留民团外交交涉委员会举行会议，讨论一等兵中山被杀案。关于该谋杀案，决定将此事宜交由日本当局处理，所有居留民应安心从事各自业务。
关于南京路事件，决定请求惩处事发地附近执勤的警察，因其玩忽职守且未能实施任何逮捕，并请求惩处监督这些警察的警官。

Nichi Nichi:-

JAPANESE BOY ASSAULTED BY CHINESE

A Japanese boy named G. Tomizo(?), a
student of the Japanese school on North Szecnuen road,
residing at No.13, San Yih Li, was assaulted by
several Chinese students in the vicinity of the Jukong

JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE ACTIVE

continued incidents, the Japanese Consular Police
have mobilized all available members of the force to
make inquiries regarding the incidents and to prevent

Yesterday at the Japanese Consular
Court a Korean named Pak Tai Hyun, age 27, was sentenced
to 25 days imprisonment for having stolen a bicycle
belonging to a Japanese, Kagei Yoko, on November 10.

《日日新闻》：-

日本男孩遭中国人殴打

一名名叫G. Tomizo(?)的日本男孩，系北四川路日本学校学生，居住在三义里13号，昨晚8时在回家途中，于虬江路市场附近遭到几名中国学生殴打。当时现场有一名中国警察，但他未试图阻止殴打行为。

日本领事警察活跃

由于连续发生事件导致不安情绪加剧，日本领事警察已动员所有可用警力，调查相关事件并防止此类事件再次发生，同时制止当前流传的谣言。领事警察将与日本海军登陆部队和工部局警务处合作执行这些任务。

朝鲜籍自行车窃贼被起诉

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, NOVEMBER 15, 1935

False War Rumours Scored
By Japanese Press Here

Tales Of Chinese Concentrations, Strengthening
Of Japan's Landing Forces Deplored;
Whampoa Officers Are Blamed

Chinese rumour-mongers, whose activities in September and October have caused a general uneasiness, were hit in an editorialized news article in the Shanghai "Mainichi" yesterday.
The list of false reports disseminated by the Chinese, the paper said, included rumours that:
1.—The Japanese forces in Tientsin are attempting to divorce the five northern provinces from China.
2.—The Kwantung Army is planning to occupy Hopei and place the province under the authority of Emperor Kangte.
3.—Rumours prevalent before the recent conference of military and diplomatic officials in Shanghai said that the Japanese navy schemed to occupy Swatow, while the Japanese Garrison in Formosa wanted to invade South China.
4.—The Japanese Third Fleet landed marines in Yuechow, Hunan, to hold manoeuvres, simultaneously threatening the anti-Communist forces in Szechwan.
5.—A Chinese army of 300,000 has been concentrated in Chekiang to prepare for a war on Japan.
6.—Forts are being constructed, under the supervision of two foreigners in Kianyin, some 20 miles north of Wusih. Japanese marines have already landed in Kianyin.
7.—General Chiang Kai-shek is ready to open war on Japan, with Nanking as the first line of defence, Kiukiang as the second, and Hankow as the last.
8.—The Japanese landing party here has been strengthened by the addition of 2,000 men.
The "Mainichi" also gave a list of instances which demonstrated the effect of these rumours on the public mind. These included the transfer of officials' families into the interior, removal of property to supposedly safer regions and suspension of commercial activities.
The paper said that Central Army officers, especially those who have graduated from the Whampoa Military Academy, are spreading groundless rumours, in effort to cause war with Japan.
Note was also taken by the "Mainichi" of the reports that construction of additional barracks in Tanahan, Nanking, was suddenly suspended, and plans made for the transfer of buildings farther back into the interior.
Forts are being hurriedly built along the Nanking-Shanghai and the Hangchow-Shanghai lines, while the establishment attached to the Hangchow and Nanyang aerodromes are being transferred into the interior, the paper added.

日本在沪报刊驳斥虚假战争谣言

哀叹有关中国军队集结及日本登陆部队增强的传闻；指责黄埔军官

昨日，上海《每日新闻》（Mainichi）在一篇带有社论性质的新闻文章中，抨击了那些在九月和十月间活动并引起普遍不安的中国造谣者。
该报称，中国人散布的虚假报告清单包括以下谣言：
1.—驻天津的日军正试图使北方五省脱离中国。
2.—关东军正计划占领河北，并将该省置于康德皇帝（Emperor Kangte）的管辖之下。
3.—在近期上海军政官员会议之前盛传的谣言称，日本海军图谋占领汕头，而台湾的日本守备队则欲入侵华南。
4.—日本第三舰队陆战队在湖南岳阳登陆举行演习，同时威胁四川的反共力量。
5.—一支三十万人的中国军队已集结于浙江，准备对日作战。
6.—在无锡以北约二十里的江阴，两名外国人监督下正在修筑炮台。日本陆战队已在江阴登陆。
7.—蒋介石将军准备对日开战，以南京为第一道防线，九江为第二道防线，汉口为最后防线。
8.—驻沪日本登陆部队增加了两千人，实力得到加强。
《每日新闻》还列举了一些实例，以证明这些谣言对公众心理的影响。其中包括官员家属迁往内地，将财产转移至所谓更安全的地区，以及商业活动的停顿。
该报称，中央军军官，特别是那些毕业于黄埔军校的人，正在散布毫无根据的谣言，企图引发对日战争。
《每日新闻》还注意到有关南京谭家山（Tanahan，音译）额外兵营建设突然停工，并计划将建筑物进一步向内地转移的报道。
该报补充说，沿宁沪线和杭沪线正在匆忙修建炮台，而与杭州和南阳机场相关的设施正在向内地转移。

CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, NOVEMBER 15, 1935

CANDOR

THE conscientious disapproval
of current rumors in Shang-
hai as voiced editorially by The
Shanghai Mainichi on November
13 is heartily endorsed by this
journal. The duty of the press to
lead, rather than be led by, public
opinion is never greater than in
such a serious crisis as confronts
this country today. Coming as it
does from a leading Japanese
daily, the disapproval is doubly
significant. It may perhaps be as-
sumed that the desire among the
Japanese community for the pre-
servation of local peace is as
sincere as that of the Chinese, and
accordingly nothing more can be
asked of them in the interest of
all residents concerned.

In the long list of rumors
enumerated may be mentioned the
one about the alleged Japanese at-
tempt to divorce the five northern
provinces from the rest of China
and to place the province of Hopei
under the rule of "Emperor
Kwangte."

This rumor, although it is de-
precated by The Mainichi, was not
untraceable to certain irresponsi-
ble statements uttered by certain
military leaders. It is fortunate
that both the Chinese and the
Japanese immediately charged with
the task of maintaining Sino-
Japanese amity have taken little
stock in its authenticity and have
allowed it to pass as mere fabrica-
tion unworthy of serious con-
sideration. Once discredited direct-
ly by the Japanese it may be laid
to rest for good.

More close at home is the
rumor about the alleged concentra-
tion of Chinese military forces in
Chekiang for the purpose of
waging a war on Japan under the
leadership of General Chiang Kai-
shek with Nanking as the first
line of defense, Kiukiang as the
second and Hankow as the last.

The presence of Chinese
troops on Chinese soil is but a
normal phenomenon. Whether
they are stationed in Shanghai or
in far away Szechwan, their move-
ment from time to time is no
ground for any complaint against
any one, and still less against
any nation. In fact, any minister
might well be called upon to
defend his country's interests
above board. The real question
is whether the movement is for
peaceful purposes. With

the purpose of their movement
understood by the Japanese, a
grave cause for apprehension is
happily removed.

With The Mainichi do we also
agree that the spread of rumors
may have caused the two regret-
table incidents on Darroch Road
and Nanking Road, upon which
this journal commented yesterday
at length.

The only point which our con-
temporary should have touched
upon is the source from which
these rumors usually originate.
Try as we may, we cannot honestly
form a definite opinion on this all-
important phase of the issue.
Speculators who are most apt to
profit by the confusion caused by
rumors may be perhaps held partly
responsible for the mischief from
which Shanghai has been suffer-
ing. The jingoist elements among
different national groups may
have also been guilty of commis-
sion. And not the least of all may
be included a part of the press and
news agencies which have lent
themselves to the propagation of
disastrous rumors.

If The Mainichi should suc-
ceed in instilling a sense of candor
in the journalistic fraternity in the
Far East, the cause of peace and
goodwill will be well served
indeed.

《大美晚报》，1935年11月15日，星期五

坦诚

本报衷心赞同《上海每日新闻》于11月13日通过社论表达的、对上海当前谣言的认真谴责。在如今国家面临的如此严重危机中，媒体引导舆论而非被舆论所左右的责任比以往任何时候都更为重大。由于这一谴责来自一家主要的日本日报，其意义加倍重要。或许可以认为，日本侨民社区希望维持地方和平的愿望与中国人一样真诚，因此，为了所有相关居民的利益，对他们不能再有更高的要求了。

在 enumerated 的长长谣言列表中，可以提到关于日本企图使北方五省脱离中国其余部分，并将河北省置于“康德皇帝”统治之下的说法。

尽管《每日新闻》对此谣言表示谴责，但它并非无法追溯到某些军事领导人发表的不负责任言论。幸运的是，直接负有维持中日友好任务的中日双方并未轻信其真实性，而是将其视为不值得认真考虑的纯粹捏造。一旦遭到日本方面的直接否认，它或许就可以永远平息了。

更为贴近本地的谣言是关于中国军队在浙江集结的说法，据称目的是在蒋介石将军的领导下对日作战，以南京为第一道防线，九江为第二道防线，汉口为最后防线。

中国军队出现在中国领土上只是一种正常现象。无论他们驻扎在上海还是遥远的四川，他们的不时调动不能成为对任何人、更不用说对任何国家提出抱怨的理由。事实上，任何部长都可能被要求公开捍卫其国家的利益。真正的问题在于这种调动是否出于和平目的。随着日本人理解了其调动的目的，一个令人严重担忧的原因 fortunately 被消除了。

我们也同意《每日新闻》的观点，即谣言的传播可能导致了达罗克路（Darroch Road）和南京路上发生的两起令人遗憾的事件，本报昨日已对此进行了详细评论。

我们的同行本应触及的唯一要点是这些谣言通常的来源。尽管我们尽力尝试，但我们无法诚实地就这一问题的所有重要方面形成明确的意见。那些最有可能从谣言造成的混乱中获利的投机者，或许应对上海一直遭受的祸害负部分责任。不同民族群体中的沙文主义分子也可能犯有此类罪行。此外，部分媒体和通讯社助长了灾难性谣言的传播，其责任也不容忽视。

如果《每日新闻》能够成功地在远东新闻界灌输一种坦诚感，那么和平与善意的事业将确实得到很好的促进。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 14, 1935

SENSE OF PROPORTION
Mr Itaro Ishii's desire for calmness will be cordially endorsed by public opinion which considers that recent events in Shanghai have been given an importance much beyond their intrinsic significance. The nervous tension created by the tragedy on Saturday night has been now accentuated by another incident about which extravagant language has been used. Given a situation such as developed by the precipitate actions and announcement of the Japanese Landing Party, and the commotion evidently aroused in the administrations of the two Municipal areas, it was inevitable that mischief-makers would find an opportunity for indulging their peculiar propensities. The Chinese Government has long ago shown its stern disapproval of anti-Japanese organizations and has taken effective steps to suppress them. No Government in the world could undertake entirely to eliminate the irresponsible individual who is prone to take advantage of a passing wave of excitement for embarrassing duly-constituted authority. The question is whether the Japanese and Chinese diplomats in pursuing their beneficent labours for rapprochement are to show the white feather merely because a common enemy heaves a brick, an empty beer-bottle and two cold-cream jars through a Japanese shop-window. The ebullition might have occurred in any City in the world and with equal success in avoiding police detection. If the stupidity had any purpose behind it, it was intended to aggravate feeling at a critical moment. The Japanese authorities will be playing into the miscreant's hands if they persist in treating it out of its proper perspective. This does not imply that the police authorities should abate their efforts to bring the perpetrators to book. They should be assisted and exhorted to that end, but they should be allowed to conduct their investigations without the irksome feeling that the affair has reached the plane of high diplomatic cognizance.
The Japanese are honoured partners in the International Settlement. It is disappointing, therefore, to find their official representatives, betrayed, unwittingly perhaps, by the heat of the moment, into action and speech which might be interpreted as neglectful of the authority of the Shanghai Municipal Council. In recent years considerable latitude has been given by the Council to the activities of the Japanese Naval Landing Party and the Japanese Consular Police. There has been no intention to abdicate the functions which are assigned to the Council's officers, although, in the interests of international good-will and out of regard for the susceptibilities of Japanese citizens, a tolerant construction has been placed on the working arrangement subsisting between the Municipal and the purely Japanese-controlled forces for preserving law and order. The Japanese authorities might find it convenient to review the situation and consider whether they are not in danger of disturbing Shanghai international harmony if their own naval and consular police are encouraged to accept too onerous a share of responsibility in Settlement affairs. When the mere threat of action by the Landing Party accompanied by the mobilization of its full strength—is found to create a minor panic leading to the hurried influx of Chinese refugees into the Settlement, it is obvious that an anomalous condition has been allowed to develop. The issue ceases to lie exclusively between Chinese and Japanese; it concerns the welfare of all communities who rely on the preservation of a proper international spirit of co-operation and tolerance in an International Settlement
No-one will associate the fiery comments of a section of the Japanese community with the balanced judgment of that community as a whole. Mr. Ishii and Rear-Admiral Sadaaki Araki are not likely to be misled by such fustian. Yet its power for mischief has to be seriously regarded when incidents are unduly magnified and made the subject of strongly-worded pronouncements. Unless a better sense of proportion be encouraged there is a danger of creating just the very situation which the Japanese authorities profess to apprehend and against which the Shanghai Municipal Council desires to guard. This is said with no pretension to assign blame to any one community. It is probably true that circumstances have led all communities to lose touch with actualities. This journal, in its desire to establish the relevant facts, has been forced to give to recent events an otherwise unjustified prominence. Is it not possible, therefore, for companionship in error to reflect dispassionately on the means of restoring equilibrium—of the senses and of judgment? The Chinese authorities have shown in a remarkable degree their capacity for restraint and calmness. The Settlement administration—in which Japanese share with other foreigners as well as with Chinese—an honourable responsibility — has spared no effort to vindicate its solicitude for the preservation of order. The general feeling in Shanghai is essentially pacific in tone and intention. There seems to be every reason for the Japanese community to dismiss uneasy thoughts and to recognize that, in contributing to the traditions of international concord on which Shanghai prides itself, it can command unreserved comradeship, sympathy and respect. In that light its anxieties may be readily dissolved.

《字林西报》，1935年11月14日，星期四

分寸感

石井伊太郎（Itaro Ishii，音译）先生对冷静的渴望将得到公众舆论的热心支持，公众舆论认为，最近上海发生的事件被赋予了远超其内在重要性的意义。周六晚间的悲剧所造成的紧张情绪，现已因另一起使用了夸张言辞的事件而加剧。鉴于日本登陆部队仓促的行动和公告所造成的局势，以及显然在两个市政区行政机构中引起的骚动，滋事者不可避免地会找到机会放纵其特殊的倾向。中国政府早已表明其对反日组织的严厉反对，并采取了有效措施予以镇压。世界上没有任何政府能够完全消除那些不负责任的个人，这些人倾向于利用一时的兴奋浪潮来为难合法成立的当局。问题在于，中日外交官在从事促进和睦的有益工作时，是否仅仅因为一个共同的敌人向一家日本商店橱窗扔了一块砖头、一个空啤酒瓶和两个冷霜罐，就要表现出怯懦。这种冲动可能发生在世界上的任何城市，并且同样成功地避开了警方的侦测。如果这种愚蠢行为背后有任何目的，那就是意在关键时刻加剧情绪。如果日本当局坚持不按适当的视角处理此事，他们就是在帮恶棍的忙。这并不意味着警察当局应放松将肇事者绳之以法的努力。应当为此目的协助并敦促他们，但应允许他们在进行调查时，不必感到此事已上升到高级外交关注的层面，从而产生厌烦情绪。

日本人是国际公共租界中受尊重的合作伙伴。因此，令人失望的是，发现他们的官方代表——也许是不知不觉地被一时的热情所背叛——采取了可能被解释为忽视上海工部局权威的言行。近年来，工部局给予日本海军登陆部队和日本领事警察的活动相当大的自由度。虽然出于国际善意的考虑以及对日本公民敏感性的尊重，对工部局与纯由日本控制的部队之间为维持治安而存在的工作安排采取了宽容的解释，但这无意放弃赋予工部局官员的职能。日本当局或许会发现，审视一下局势并考虑如果他们自己的海军和领事警察被鼓励承担租界事务中过于繁重的责任份额，是否会有破坏上海国际和谐的危险，这样做是方便的。当仅仅由登陆部队采取行动并动员其全部兵力的威胁就被发现造成轻微恐慌，导致中国难民匆忙涌入租界时，显而易见，一种反常的状况已被允许发展。这个问题不再仅仅存在于中日之间；它关系到所有社区的幸福，这些社区依赖于在国际公共租界中保持适当的国际合作和宽容精神。

没有人会将日本社区部分成员的激烈评论与该社区整体的平衡判断联系起来。石井先生和荒木贞孝（Sadaaki Araki，音译）海军少将不太可能被这种浮夸之词所误导。然而，当事件被过度放大并成为措辞强烈的声明的主题时，其制造祸害的能力必须得到严肃对待。除非鼓励更好的分寸感，否则就有可能造成日本当局声称担心且上海工部局希望防范的那种局面。这样说并非妄图指责任何一个社区。情况可能导致所有社区都脱离了现实，这可能是真的。本报出于确立相关事实的愿望，不得不给予最近事件 otherwise 不合理的突出地位。因此，共同犯错的朋友难道不可能冷静地反思恢复平衡——感官和判断力的平衡——的手段吗？中国当局以显著的程度展示了他们的克制和冷静能力。租界行政机构——日本人与其他外国人以及中国人共同分担这一光荣责任——已不遗余力地证明其对维持秩序的关切。上海的总体情绪在基调和意图上本质上是和平的。日本社区似乎有充分理由摒弃不安的想法，并认识到，在为上海引以为豪的国际协和传统做出贡献方面，它可以赢得毫无保留的伙伴情谊、同情和尊重。从这个角度来看，其焦虑很容易消散。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 14, 1935

SUPPRESSION OF ANTI-JAPAN
ACTIVITIES DEMANDED

Tokyo's Protest Presented to Nanking Over Local
Incidents: Regret Expressed

CHINA PLEDGES SINCERE MEASURES

Nanking Nov 13
Complete suppression of anti-Japanese movements by the Nanking Government to prevent the recurrence of attacks on Japanese lives and property, was urged this morning by an official of the Consulate-General here, in an interview with Mr. Kao Tsung-wu, Chief of the Asiatic Affairs Section of the Waichiaopu.
Mr. Motoki Matsumura, third secretary of the Japanese Embassy in China, representing Mr. Yakichiro Suma, Consul-General here, called at the Waichiaopu on instructions from Mr. Koki Hirota, the Foreign Minister.
Citing the murder of a Japanese sailor and the attack on a Japanese shop in Shanghai, Mr. Matsumura is said to have expressed deep regret over the failure of the Chinese authorities to suppress the anti-Japanese movement. This, he said, was especially regrettable in view of the recent improvement in Sino-Japanese relations.
Replying to Mr. Matsumura, Mr. Kao gave a pledge that strict and sincere measures will be taken to put an end to the anti-Japanese movement, adding that the Municipal Government of Greater Shanghai was actively engaged in the search for the culprits, in co-operation with the Shanghai Municipal Council.
Mr. Suma will return here tomorrow from Shanghai to conduct formal negotiations on the issue with Mr. Tang Yu-jen, Vice-Minister for Foreign Affairs.—Rengo.

Concern in Tokyo
Tokyo, Nov. 13.
While a temporary lull exists in news received from Shanghai and north China, anxiety here over anti-Japanese activities in China has not slackened.
All circles are now awaiting the reactions of the Nanking Government to the Foreign Office protest, which may be delivered to-morrow.
Japanese press reports from Shanghai indicate that Japanese officials there consider the efforts of both the Shanghai Municipal Police and the Bureau of Public Safety of Greater Shanghai as desultory, as regards the apprehension of the assassin of the Japanese blue-jacket, Hideo Nakayama, last Saturday night. Accordingly, Japanese naval authorities may possibly conduct an independent investigation of the case and search Chinese houses adjacent to the scene of the assassination.
No anti-Japanese activities have been reported in the last twenty-four hours, but should they be resumed anywhere in China, it is generally predicted that the Japanese Army and Navy in China will stiffen their attitude considerably.
The Foreign Office declared to-day that the Japanese Consul-General at Nanking, Mr. Y. Suma, would probably confer with Chinese officials before presenting the formal note of protest, which may be held for a brief period, during which the Japanese will observe and study the situation.

No Other Demands
The acting spokesman of the Foreign Office, Mr. Satoh, said that the report that Japan was presenting demands beyond the request for an immediate cessation of anti-Japanese activities were "not true."
Again asked whether the Japanese were certain that the activity at Shanghai would not produce results similar to the hostilities of 1932, the spokesman replied, "That depends on future developments." This answer was regarded by some observers as indicating that the Japanese Government is taking a more serious view of the situation than it did earlier in the week.
In connection with reports received here concerning movements for the establishment of autonomous governments at many points in north China, some Tokyo observers believe that the Kwantung Army might assist such movements if the Nanking Government attempts to suppress them by force.
The Changchun correspondent of the Nippon Dempo News Agency predicted that the Kwantung Army plans "some kind of action in its line of duty" within two days. He added that recent anti-Japanese activities were "very similar to the series of incidents preceding the 1932 conflict."—United Press.

《字林西报》，1935年11月14日，星期四

要求镇压反日活动

就当地事件向南京提出东京抗议：表示遗憾

中国承诺采取真诚措施

南京，11月13日
今晨，日本驻沪总领事馆一名官员在拜访外交部亚洲司司长高宗武先生时，敦促南京政府彻底镇压反日运动，以防止袭击日本人生命和财产的事件再次发生。
日本驻华大使馆三等秘书松村元木（Motoki Matsumura，音译）代表驻沪总领事须磨弥吉郎（Yakichiro Suma）先生，奉外相广田弘毅（Koki Hirota）先生之命，前往外交部拜会。
据称，松村先生援引一名日本水兵被杀及上海一家日商店铺遭袭之事，对中国当局未能镇压反日运动深表遗憾。他说，鉴于近期中日关系的改善，这种情况尤其令人遗憾。
高先生答复松村先生时承诺，将采取严格而真诚的措施以结束反日运动，并补充说，上海特别市政府正与工部局合作，积极搜捕罪犯。——联合通讯社

须磨先生将于明日从上海返回此处，就此事与外交部次长唐有壬先生进行正式谈判。——联合同盟社

东京方面的关切
东京，11月13日。
虽然从上海和华北收到的消息出现暂时的平静，但此处对中国境内反日活动的焦虑并未减轻。
各界目前正在等待南京政府对可能于明日递交的外务省抗议书的反应。
据日本报纸从上海发回的报道，那里的日本官员认为，关于上周六晚遇害的日本水兵中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）一案，上海公共租界工部局警务处和上海特别市公安局在逮捕凶手方面的努力均显得漫不经心。因此，日本海军当局可能会对此案进行独立调查，并搜查暗杀现场附近的中国民居。
过去二十四小时内未报告有反日活动，但如果中国任何地方恢复此类活动，普遍预测在华日本陆海军将大幅强硬其态度。
外务省今日声明，驻南京日本总领事须磨弥吉郎（Y. Suma）先生在递交正式抗议照会之前，可能会先与中国官员会晤；该照会可能会暂缓片刻递交，在此期间，日方将观察和研究局势。

无其他要求
外务省代理发言人佐藤（Satoh，音译）先生表示，有关日本除了要求立即停止反日活动之外还提出其他要求的报道“不属实”。
当再次被问及日本方面是否确信上海的活动不会产生类似1932年敌对行动的结果时，该发言人回答说：“这取决于未来的发展。”一些观察家认为，这一回答表明日本政府比本周初更严肃地看待当前局势。
结合此处收到的关于华北多地建立自治政府运动的报告，一些东京观察家认为，如果南京政府试图以武力镇压这些运动，关东军可能会协助此类运动。
日本电报通讯社长春记者预测，关东军计划在两天内“在其职责范围内采取某种行动”。他补充说，近期的反日活动“与1932年冲突前的一系列事件非常相似”。——合众社

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
Sp. Branch XXXXX
Date November 13, 1935

REPORT

Subject Movement of Chinese Troops.

Made by D. S. Mac Adie Forwarded by (签名)

According to a reliable foreign witness who has
just returned from a motor caravan tour of Kiangsu,
Chekiang and the borders of Kiangsi Provinces, there are
no concentrations of Chinese troops in southern Kiangsu.
At Kashing, however, a division arrived nine days ago.
The witness conversed with some of these men and was told
that they had been fighting in Kiangsi for the last
eighteen months and had been transferred to Kashing for
a rest. They had with them twenty Vickers caterpillar
armoured cars . These vehicles were comparatively new and
in good condition. Witness was asked for assistance in
clearing a blocked petrol feed pipe of one of these cars.
In Chekiang south of Hangchow and on the borders of
Kiangsi, bandits were numerous and there were many troops
in that region.

During the last week, the witness was in the neigh-
bourhood of Nanziang, Quinsan and the area immediately
to the west of Shanghai; his information, therefore, is
quite recent. The motor caravan stopped in large towns and
villages and gave cinema shows for advertisement purposes.
The witness has travelled in the interior for many years
and speaks the language and so his observations should
be of value.

In view of the rumours of troop concentration in the
environs of Shanghai, the above information may be of
interest.

Good information.
File JAS.
R. W. Mac Adie
D. S.

D. C. (Special Branch).

据一位刚从江苏、浙江及江西边境进行汽车巡回宣传归来、可靠的外国目击者称，苏南地区没有中国军队集结。
然而，九天前有一个师抵达嘉兴。目击者与其中一些士兵交谈，得知他们在过去十八个月里一直在江西作战，后被调至嘉兴休整。他们随队携带了二十辆维克斯履带式装甲车。这些车辆较新且状况良好。目击者曾受邀协助疏通其中一辆车的堵塞燃油管。
在杭州以南的浙江地区及江西边境，匪患严重，该地区驻有大量军队。

上周，目击者在南翔、昆山及上海紧邻西部区域活动；因此，他的信息相当近期。该车队在较大的城镇和村庄停留，并放映电影以作宣传。
该目击者在中国内地旅行多年，通晓语言，因此他的观察应具有价值。

鉴于有关上海周边军队集结的谣言，上述信息可能具有参考价值。

情报良好。
归档 JAS。
R. W. Mac Adie
D. S.

Subject: Military Movements Around Shanghai.

Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pih    Forwarded by [Signature]

Local foreign newspapers recently published reports
alleging that large detachments of Chinese troops were
concentrated near the Lunghwa and Hungjao Airfields as well
as other places on the boundary of the demilitarized zone
around Shanghai. On November 8, 1935, enquiries were made
by D.I. Pan Lien-pih in the vicinity of Lunghwa, Hungjao, and
Chenju, but no concentration of troops was observed.
It has been ascertained, however, that military
police are billeted at Lunghwa and Kaochonmiao, and that
members of the Peace Preservation Corps, numbering 3,300, are
posted at various places in Shanghai and its surroundings.
A further report will be submitted in due course on
the movements of Chinese military at places beyond Shanghai
along the Nanking-Shanghai Railway and the Shanghai-Hangchow-

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 7. 1935

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
POLICE REGISTRY

MILITARY MOVEMENTS
CLOSELY WATCHED

Japanese Allege Concentrations
Round Shanghai

Japanese military authorities in
Shanghai are paying close attention to
the alleged heavy concentrations of
Chinese troops on the edge of the
demilitarized zone around Shanghai
established after the hostilities of
1932, the "Shanghai Nichi-Nichi" said
yesterday. Heavy detachments are
near Lunghua and Hungjao airfields.
The Chinese forces were moved up
from their recent positions along the
Shanghai-Hangchow-Ningpo Railway
where they have been stationed for
several weeks, the daily added.
Chinese authorities are explaining
the concentrations as a precautionary
move to prevent any disturbances that
may arise from the enforcement of
monetary reforms, according to the
"Nichi-Nichi."

Made by D.S. McKeown Forwarded by [签名]

H.I.J.M.S. "Urakaze" arrived at the C.S.K. Wharf,
Yangtszepoo Road, at 11 a.m. November 28, and discharged
460 boxes believed to contain ammunition. The boxes are
now stored in the wharf godown. The warship crossed to
the Pootung side in the afternoon where it is now berthed at
the M.B.K. Wharf.

The report that H.I.J.M. troopship "Muroto" is
in Shanghai has not been confirmed but it is learned that
this vessel is expected to arrive at any time for the purpose
of conveying a number of marines from Shanghai to Japan.

following information has been obtained :-

Shanghai-Nanking Railway Line between Shanghai and Soochow

The nearest city to Shanghai on this line where
troops are stationed is Anting (安亭), which is approximately
19 miles from Shanghai. At this point 378 soldiers of the
2nd Battalion, 9th Regiment of the Military Police are
collected. This unit was transferred from Quinsan in the
middle of October. The number of troops between Anting
and Soochow is estimated at 3,000, which figure constitutes
an increase of 1,500 above the normal strength. Statistics
showing the disposition of troops, their units, and strength,
at cities between Anting and Soochow are attached as
Appendix "A".

approximately 28 miles from Shanghai. In this city there

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, November 7, 1935

Large Assemblage
Of Troops Draws
Japanese Interest

100,000 Said Gathered
In Shanghai, Hangchow
Nanking Areas

NO ALARM FELT
SAY SPOKESMEN

Considered Merely Item
In Domestic Policies;
Two Explanations

With many completely unconfirm-
ed reports in circulation concerning
changes in General Chiang Kai-
shek's policy toward Japan, much
interest centered today on the
allegedly huge concentration of
troops in the Shanghai, Hangchow
and Nanking areas.

Japanese military authorities stat-
ed today that the troops in these
areas comprised six or seven divi-
sions, totaling approximately 100,-
000. It was stated in both Japanese
military and diplomatic circles that
the concentration was being care-
fully watched.

A Domestic Matter

While many Chinese, notably
those who have long opposed Gen-
eral Chiang, appear to think that
the future trend of his policy will
be anti-Japanese, including possibly
even a "holy war" against Japan,
the Japanese themselves profess to
regard the troop concentration as
merely an item in domestic politics
and in no way directed against
them.

Two explanations are given by
Japanese spokesmen: preservation
of peace and order during the sixth
preliminary session of the Central
Executive Committee of the Kuo-
mintang and the forthcoming
scheduled congress of the Kuomin-
tang, and enforcement of the na-
tionalization of railways.

Jiang, says Japanese Spokesmen

These separate officials assert
that Nanjing plans to seize after
which is not voluntarily surrender-
ed, but this is denied by Chinese
officials. There is admittedly a
large amount of silver not held in
banks, but buried or otherwise
secreted in private homes. How-
ever, Chinese officials say that no
military action is contemplated to
obtain possession of it.

The troop concentration started
shortly before the C.E.C. session
and troops are stationed in various
cities along the Shanghai-Nanking
and Shanghai-Hangchow railways.
A large number are said to be in
the vicinity of Wusong and Hung-
jao, but none according to the
Japanese, have entered the de-
militarized zone around Shanghai.

History Of Zone

This demilitarized zone, extend-
ing about 20 miles from the bound-
aries of the foreign concessions, was
created by the Sino-Japanese peace
pact of May 5, 1932, after the con-
clusion of the Shanghai warfare.
This pact is without a time limit,
and Chinese troops are prohibited
from entering this zone during the
period of its duration.

An international committee, in-
cluding Chinese and Japanese, was
set up for the enforcement of the
pact and is still in existence. It
has never, however, held but one
session, which was shortly after the
pact was concluded and was for
the purpose of permitting Chinese
safety preservation corps to enter
the zone.

Provocation Disavowed

One Japanese official said today
that should any Chinese troops
enter the demilitarized zone, the
fact would be immediately called to
the attention of the international
committee. But any anti-Japanese
purpose in the troop concentration
was disavowed, as was also the re-
port of any anti-Japanese trend in
General Chiang's policy.

The troop concentration, the
Japanese reported, has caused a
considerable influx of Chinese from
nearby towns into China. There
has also been some influx of Chin-
ese from Chapei and Hongkew into
the foreign areas south of Soochow
Creek during the past few days.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1935年11月7日，星期四

大量军队
集结引起
日本关注

据称十万大军
集结于上海、杭州
南京地区

发言人称
并无恐慌

被视为内政之一项；
两种解释

随着关于蒋介石将军对日政策变动的诸多完全未经证实的消息流传，今日的焦点集中在据称于上海、杭州和南京地区的大规模军队集结上。

日本军方当局今日表示，这些地区的部队包括六七个师，总计约10万人。日本军方和外交界均表示，正在密切监视此次集结。

内政事务

虽然许多中国人，特别是那些长期反对蒋将军的人，似乎认为其政策的未来趋势将是反日的，甚至可能包括对日发动“圣战”，但日本人自己声称，将此次军队集结仅视为国内政治的一项内容，绝非针对他们。

日本发言人给出了两种解释：一是在国民党第六届中央执行委员会预备会议及即将召开的国民党代表大会期间维持治安秩序；二是推行铁路国有化。

日本发言人谈及白银问题

这些个别官员声称，南京计划夺取未自愿上交的白银，但这遭到中国官员的否认。诚然，有大量白银未存入银行，而是埋藏或以其他秘密方式藏匿于私人住宅中。然而，中国官员表示，并未考虑采取军事行动来获取这些白银。

此次军队集结始于中执会会议前不久，部队驻扎在沪宁和沪杭铁路沿线的各个城市。据称大量部队位于吴淞和虹桥附近，但据日方称，没有一兵一卒进入上海周边的非军事区。

非军事区的历史

该非军事区从外国租界边界向外延伸约20英里，是根据1932年5月5日结束上海战事的中日和平协定设立的。该协定没有期限限制，在其有效期内禁止中国军队进入该区域。

为执行该协定，成立了一个包括中日双方在内的国际委员会，该委员会至今仍然存在。然而，它只召开过一次会议，那是在协定缔结后不久，目的是允许中国保安队进入该区域。

否认挑衅

一位日本官员今日表示，如有任何中国军队进入非军事区，将立即提请国际委员会注意。但他否认此次军队集结有任何反日目的，也否认了有关蒋将军政策出现任何反日趋势的报道。

日方报道，此次军队集结导致附近城镇的中国人大量涌入中国（内地）。此外，在过去几天里，也有一些中国人从闸北和虹口流入苏州河以南的外国区域。

North China Daily News - Nov.7, 1935

MILITARY MOVEMENTS
CLOSELY WATCHED
—— 7/11/35
Japanese Allege Concentrations
Round Shanghai

Japanese military authorities in
Shanghai are paying close attention to
the alleged heavy concentrations of
Chinese troops on the edge of the
demilitarized zone around Shanghai
established after the hostilities of
1932, the "Shanghai Nichi-Nichi" said
yesterday. Heavy detachments are
near Lunghua and Hungjao airfields.
The Chinese forces were moved up
from their recent positions along the
Shanghai-Hangchow-Ningpo Railway
where they have been stationed for
several weeks, the daily added.
Chinese authorities are explaining
the concentrations as a precautionary
move to prevent any disturbances that
may arise from the enforcement of
monetary reforms, according to the
"Nichi-Nichi."

《字林西报》 - 1935年11月7日

军事调动
受到严密监视
—— 1935年11月7日
日方称上海周边有军队集结

《上海日日新闻》昨日称，上海日本军方当局正密切关注据称在1932年敌对行动后建立的上海周边非军事区边缘的中国军队大规模集结。大批分队位于龙华和虹桥机场附近。该日报补充说，中国军队是从最近几周驻守的沪杭甬铁路沿线阵地调上来的。
据《日日新闻》称，中国当局解释称，此次集结是为防止因实施货币改革而可能引发的任何骚乱所采取的预防措施。
